children: Taiwan’s annual inflation rate rose to 2.7% in September 2026 from 2.05% in the previous month.

It marked the highest level since February 2024 and the fifth consecutive month above the central bank’s 2% target, as food prices accelerated sharply, advancing to a one-year high of 2.64% from 0.77% in August. Inflation also climbed for transportation and communication (4.07% vs 2.79%), as well as clothing (2.32% vs 2.09%), housing (2.38% vs 2.31%), and healthcare (0.70% vs 0.57%).
Meanwhile, price growth moderated slightly in education and entertainment (3.15% vs 3.22%), and miscellaneous goods and services (2.77% vs 2.81%).
On a seasonally adjusted monthly basis, consumer prices eased to 0.13% from 0.19% in August, marking the lowest reading since November 2025.

title: Taiwan Inflation Hits 31-Month High
